intended_object: The canonical natural isomorphism, over all commutative K-algebras R, between the group of invertible upper-triangular matrices T_n(R) and the group of R-points Hom_K(Spec R, T_n) of the affine upper-triangular group scheme T_n = Spec(O(GL_n)/(x_ij : j<i)). In other words, the statement that this group scheme represents the functor R ↦ T_n(R) (Milne, Algebraic Groups, §§2.8–2.9). I took this from the docstring and the surrounding module.
explanation:
**Source functor.** `upperTriangularGroupFunctor` sends each commutative K-algebra R to `Matrix.UpperTriangularGroup n R`. This is the subgroup of GL_n(R) of matrices that are `IsUpperTriangular`, which is the standard T_n(R). On morphisms it applies the algebra map entrywise.

**Target functor.** It is algSpec followed by the Yoneda group functor of `upperTriangularGroupScheme K n`. Its value at R is the group of K-scheme maps Spec R → Spec(CoordinateRing), with the group structure coming from the group object.

**Components.** Each component is `upperTriangularGroupMulEquivPoints`, built as the composite of two maps:
- A multiplicative equivalence T_n(R) ≃ Hom_K-alg(O(T_n), R), with the convolution product on the right. In one direction it evaluates the coordinate functions at the matrix; in the other it reads off the matrix of entries. The relations below the diagonal are exactly the ideal being quotiented out.
- `Spec.mapMulEquiv`, which turns algebra maps into scheme maps.

The naturality square is proved via `upperTriangularFromGL_natural`. This is exactly the canonical identification of the points of T_n with invertible upper-triangular matrices.

**Generality and degenerate cases.** The construction works over any commutative base ring K and any finite linearly ordered index type n. This is the natural generality for the upper-triangular group scheme (a linear order on n is needed to define "upper-triangular"). Degenerate cases (empty n, zero ring) are handled uniformly.

**Mathlib.** Mathlib has no counterpart for this group scheme or for its representability isomorphism.
